newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index falls sharply in early trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index falls sharply in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index tumbled sharply in early trade on Wednesday, dropping 151 points, or 0.92 percent, to 16,232, in a property-led decline.
"The fall is led very much by property developers," said Percy Au-Young, research director of DBS Securities.
Investors were worried U.S. interest rates might rise on inflation fears, which caused Wall Street to come down by 100 points and the bond yield to increase, he said.
The Dow industrials tumbled 101.27 points to end Tuesday at 7,960.84 and the 30-year bond fell 13/32 to yield 6.67 precent.
"Property developers are very interest-rate-sensitive so that's why the companies fall, and maybe a minor reason is that more banks have increased their mortgage rates," Au-Young said.
Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$1.75 to HK$98.25.
Cheung Kong eased HK$0.50 to HK$91.75 and Henderson Land fell HK$0.75 to HK$69.75.
"The market's focus shifted from blue chips to second line and China-related stocks such as red chips and H-shares," said Jason Tang of institutional sales at South China Securities.
Nine of the 10 most traded stocks were red chips and H-shares with only smaller-sized local firm Emperor (China) taking a seat as the eighth most active stock.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index surged 62 points, or 4.33 percent, to 1,495 in early trade. Jingwei Textile HK$0.525, or 23.86 percent, to HK$2.725.

H-shares were boosted by a restructuring concept which investors believed would lead to good quality assets being injected into the listed companies by their Chinese parents when they undergo corporate restructuring, Lui said.
Index futures-related selling was expected to continue since August contracts were trading at a good discount to the spot market, brokers said.
August futures lost 160 points at 16,130, or about a 70 point discount to the Hang Seng Index. September contracts fell 165 points to 16,210.
